figures.name: King David
figures.summary: Took another man's wife, then arranged the husband's death; confronted by Nathan, he confessed.
figures.note: Psalm 51 is Psalm 50 in Septuagint numbering; verse numbers differ by tradition.

figures.name: Peter
figures.summary: Denied knowing Jesus three times; restored by the risen Jesus with three questions of love.

figures.name: Paul (Saul)
figures.summary: Hunted and imprisoned Christians; later called himself the foremost of sinners.

figures.name: Moses
figures.summary: Killed an Egyptian and fled; God later called him from the burning bush.

figures.name: Abraham
figures.summary: Twice passed off his wife as his sister to protect himself.

figures.name: Jacob
figures.summary: Deceived his father to steal his brother's blessing; wrestled with God and reconciled with Esau.

figures.name: Jonah
figures.summary: Ran from God's call, then resented God's mercy to his enemies.

figures.name: Elijah
figures.summary: After great victory, fled in fear and asked to die; God fed him, let him rest, and spoke to him.
figures.note: Despair is not sin in itself; frame as struggle, not guilt.

figures.name: Samson
figures.summary: Gave in repeatedly to desire and pride, lost his strength and sight; prayed at the end.

figures.name: Aaron
figures.summary: Made the golden calf under pressure and made excuses; still ordained as priest.

figures.name: Rahab
figures.summary: A prostitute in Jericho who sheltered the spies; saved and later named among the faithful.

figures.name: Matthew (Levi)
figures.summary: A tax collector Jesus called to follow him, then ate with.

figures.name: Zacchaeus
figures.summary: A chief tax collector who cheated people; repaid fourfold after Jesus came to his house.

figures.name: The Samaritan woman
figures.summary: Jesus named her past plainly and she became a witness to her town.

figures.name: The woman caught in adultery
figures.summary: Jesus refused to condemn her and told her to sin no more.
figures.note: John 7:53-8:11 is absent from the earliest manuscripts; always show this note.

figures.name: Thomas
figures.summary: Refused to believe without proof; Jesus met him where he was.

figures.name: John Mark
figures.summary: Left Paul mid-mission, causing a split; later called useful by Paul.

figures.name: Nebuchadnezzar
figures.summary: Boasted in his own power, was humbled, then praised God.

figures.name: King Manasseh
figures.summary: Among the worst kings of Judah; humbled in captivity, he repented and was restored.
figures.note: Prayer of Manasseh is canonical only for orthodox / ethiopian_orthodox; filter that passage by tradition.

figures.name: St. Augustine
figures.summary: Stole pears for the thrill of it and lived for years in lust and ambition; converted in a Milan garden.

passages.match: pears
Take up and read

figures.note: Gutenberg Pusey text has no chapter numbers; refs are by Book.

figures.name: Abba Moses the Ethiopian (Black)
figures.summary: A robber and gang leader who became a monk and a father of the desert.

passages.ref: Paradise of the Holy Fathers, “NOW there was a certain man whose name…”
passages.match: Moses
Moses

figures.note: Budge's Paradise calls him 'Moses the Indian'. Tradition passages are narrowed by a content match ('Moses').

figures.name: St. Mary of Egypt
figures.summary: From the age of twelve lived for twenty-seven years in sexual sin; turned back at the door of the church in Jerusalem, she wept, and spent forty-seven years in repentance in the desert of the Jordan.

passages.match: made her to love fornication
desert of the Jordan thou wilt find rest
Bury mary, the poor woman

figures.name: Noah
figures.summary: After the flood he planted a vineyard, got drunk and lay uncovered in his tent; Scripture still remembers him among the faithful.

figures.name: The prodigal son
figures.summary: Took his inheritance and wasted it on wild living until he fed pigs; came home to a father who ran to meet him.

figures.name: Miriam
figures.summary: Spoke against her brother Moses out of jealousy and was struck with leprosy; Moses prayed for her and she was healed.

figures.name: Judah
figures.summary: Sold his brother Joseph into slavery and slept with a woman he took for a prostitute; later offered his own life for his brother Benjamin.

figures.name: Job
figures.summary: Lost everything, cursed the day he was born and accused God; God answered him out of the whirlwind and restored him.

figures.name: The penitent thief
figures.summary: A criminal crucified beside Jesus who, in his last hour, asked to be remembered, and was promised paradise that same day.

figures.name: The woman who anointed Jesus
figures.summary: Known in her town as a sinner, she washed Jesus' feet with her tears; he told her, “Your sins are forgiven.”

figures.name: Naomi
figures.summary: After losing her husband and sons she said, “Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me”; she lived to hold her grandson.

figures.name: St. Cyprian
figures.summary: A famous sorcerer who used magic to try to take a praying girl for another man; when it failed he burned his books of magic, was baptized, and died a bishop and martyr.

passages.match: teacher of sorcery
all the works of his sorcery
destroyed his books of magic

figures.note: Cyprian of Antioch, not Cyprian of Carthage. Read from the Ethiopian Synaxarium (Maskaram).

figures.name: St. Thais
figures.summary: A prostitute in Egypt who burned everything she had earned by sin in the middle of the city, and spent three years in a cell praying, “You who made me, have mercy on me.”

passages.ref: Paradise of the Holy Fathers, “AND now I desire to narrate unto you…”
passages.match: take up a position in the market

passages.ref: Paradise of the Holy Fathers, “AND now I desire to narrate unto you…”
passages.match: burnt it with fire in the midst of the city

passages.ref: Paradise of the Holy Fathers, “AND now I desire to narrate unto you…”
passages.match: This couch is not for Anthony

figures.name: St. Martha of Egypt
figures.summary: Lived openly in sexual sin in Cairo; turned away at the church door at Christmas, she burned all her wealth and spent twenty-five years in repentance in a convent.

passages.match: She loved fornication
sent her to a house for virgins

figures.name: The young man St. Basil restored
figures.summary: For the love of a woman he went to a magician and denied Christ in writing; afraid it was too late, he wept, and St. Basil prayed with him for forty days until he was free.

passages.match: denied Christ our God
Dost thou wish to return and to be a Christian once more

figures.note: Read from the Ethiopian Synaxarium (Maskaram), a miracle of St. Basil the Great.

figures.name: Abba Moses the hermit
figures.summary: After thirty-five years of holiness in the desert he was lured away by a woman and denied his faith; left to die, he wept with dust on his face, and an angel told him, “Your sin is forgiven.”

passages.match: thirty and five years
How can I who am a monk
Thy sin is remitted unto thee

figures.note: Read from the Ethiopian Synaxarium (Maskaram). Not Abba Moses the Black.

figures.name: Jacob the monk
figures.summary: A hermit of fifteen years, he fell into sin with a girl brought to him for healing, then killed her and her brother to hide it; in despair he met a monk who said, “Cut not off hope,” and after forty years of repentance God answered his prayer with rain.

passages.match: made him to fall into sin with her
he killed the woman and her brother
had accepted his prayer and his repentance

figures.name: Mary, niece of Abba Abraham
figures.summary: Raised in prayer by her uncle, she fell with a monk, left her life and went to work in a tavern; her uncle came for her in disguise, took her hand and said, “Thy sin lieth upon me… Come, return,” and she did.

passages.match: intimate terms with a certain monk
thy sin lieth upon me

figures.note: Read from the Ethiopian Synaxarium (Nahase), in the story of Abba Abraham.

figures.name: The woman who came to tempt Abba Martianus
figures.summary: She took money to make a holy hermit fall; when she found him burning his hands in a fire rather than sin, she came to herself, begged him to save her soul, and repented with all her heart.

passages.match: How much money will ye give me
she repented with all her heart

figures.note: Read from the Ethiopian Synaxarium (Genbot). The text does not give her name.

figures.name: Hero of Alexandria
figures.summary: A brilliant young monk who knew the Scriptures by heart, he fell through pride into the taverns, the theatres and drunkenness, and then into lust; broken by sickness, he came back to the desert, confessed everything to the fathers, and died repenting with tears.

passages.ref: Paradise of the Holy Fathers, “AND there was also my neighbour, a man…”
passages.match: seized by the passion of boasting and pridefulness

passages.ref: Paradise of the Holy Fathers, “AND there was also my neighbour, a man…”
passages.match: confessed all these things to the fathers

figures.note: Read from the Paradise of the Holy Fathers (Palladius), where he is called Ahron (Hero); Heron in the Lausiac History.

figures.name: The robber captain who came to Abba Daniel’s nuns
figures.summary: He disguised himself as the holy Abba Daniel to rob a convent; when a blind nun washed her face and could see, he repented and became a monk with Abba Daniel.

passages.match: captain of the thieves saw this he repented

figures.note: Read from the Ethiopian Synaxarium (Takhsas), in the story of Abba Daniel. The text does not give his name.

figures.name: The old man who envied Abba Poemen
figures.summary: When his followers left him for Abba Poemen, he was filled with envy and cursed them; Poemen came to his door with bread and waited humbly until the old man repented, opened the door, and became his friend.

passages.ref: Paradise of the Holy Fathers, “ABBA ISAAC, the priest of the Cells, used…”
passages.match: the old man was filled with envy

figures.note: Read from the Sayings of the Fathers in the Paradise of the Holy Fathers. The text does not give his name.

figures.name: The cook in Abba Gelasius’s monastery
figures.summary: In a rage over a fish he kicked a boy, who fell and died; terrified, he went and told Abba Gelasius, who laid the boy in the sanctuary, and after the evening prayer the boy walked out alive; the cook was given a penance.

passages.match: wrath came upon him, and he kicked him

figures.note: Read from the Ethiopian Synaxarium (Yakatit), in the story of Abba Gelasius. The text does not give his name.

figures.name: Zechariah
figures.summary: An old priest who, when the angel Gabriel promised him a son, asked “How can I be sure of this?” and was struck silent; when the child was born, his mouth was opened and he blessed God.

figures.name: Joseph of Arimathea
figures.summary: A rich man and a disciple of Jesus, but secretly, for fear; when Jesus had died, he went in boldly to Pilate, asked for His body, and buried Him.

figures.name: King Solomon
figures.summary: The wisest of kings, whose many wives turned his heart after other gods. The Kebra Nagast, read in the Ethiopian Church, says: “God hath had mercy upon him,” and his name is written in the Book of Life.

passages.match: God hath had mercy upon him

figures.note: His fall is Scripture (1 Kings 11); his restoration is Ethiopian tradition (Kebra Nagast, chapter 65), so he is shown to Ethiopian Orthodox readers.
